key_insight: Faculty-designed “AI-proof” college assessments remained vulnerable: the best-performing LLM scored approximately 83% without supplementary course materials and 85% with them.
engineering_relevance: AI-resistant assessment design needs empirical testing rather than relying on question complexity or instructor intuition alone.
method: Collected 75 authentic college assessment questions across 17 disciplines, including 61 intentionally designed to resist LLMs.
Evaluated three state-of-the-art LLMs with and without supplementary course materials.
Identified five faculty design strategies through thematic analysis and tested their impact on answer accuracy.
evidence_signal: The evaluation covered questions contributed by 37 faculty members from 11 U.S. and U.K. universities, alongside online-course questions, and found performance differences across models, answer formats, and design strategies.
watch_item: Results from 75 questions and three models may not generalize to all disciplines, assessment formats, or future LLMs.
paper_title: Generative AI and the Crisis of Higher Education Assessments: Examining 'AI-Proofing' Strategies for College-Level Assessments
